title: How deep is the ocean really? 😳
description:
Sinking from the surface to the deepest point on Earth, almost 11 km down. The last thing waiting at the bottom is the worst part.

0 m → 200 m → 332 m → 1,000 m → 2,992 m → 3,800 m → 4,000 m → 8,336 m → 10,935 m

Facts: deepest scuba dive, Ahmed Gabr, 332 m (2014). Cuvier's beaked whale dive, 2,992 m (2014 study). Deepest fish ever filmed, a snailfish at 8,336 m (2022). A plastic bag was recorded at 10,898 m in the Mariana Trench (JAMSTEC deep-sea debris database).

title: The ocean made a sound louder than a blue whale 🔊
description:
In 1997, Navy microphones built to hunt submarines picked up a sound nobody could explain. Sensors almost 5,000 km apart heard it. The internet decided it was a monster. In 2005, scientists finally found the answer.

Source: NOAA Pacific Marine Environmental Laboratory. The sound in this video is a recreation, not the original recording.

title: This shark could be older than America 🦈
description:
The Greenland shark can live for around 400 years. The oldest one scientists measured was about 392 years old (give or take 120). It grows 1 cm a year, isn't an adult until about 150, swims slower than you walk, and its meat can make you act drunk.

Source: Nielsen et al., Science (2016), eye-lens radiocarbon dating.

title: What really happened to the Titan sub
description:
In June 2023, five people went down to see the Titanic in the Titan submersible. An hour and 45 minutes into the dive, it went silent, and for four days the world watched an oxygen countdown. This is what had already happened, more than 3 km down.

Facts: US Coast Guard Marine Board of Investigation report on the loss of Titan. Debris found about 500 m from the Titanic's bow.
In memory of the five people on board.

title: The kraken is real 🦑
description:
Sailors told stories about the kraken for centuries. Then science found the giant squid: as long as a bus, with eyes the size of dinner plates, three hearts, blue blood and a brain shaped like a doughnut.

Facts: first photographed alive in the wild in 2004 (Kubodera & Mori, Proc. Royal Society B, 2005). First filmed in its habitat in 2012 (Japan's National Science Museum, NHK, Discovery). Eye size and anatomy from the Smithsonian Ocean Portal.

title: Everest would vanish in this ocean trench 🏔️
description:
Drop Mount Everest into the Mariana Trench and its summit would still be more than 2 km under water. The trench is 2,550 km long, the pressure at the bottom is 8 tons per square inch, and something still lives down there.

Facts: Everest 8,849 m (2020 survey). Challenger Deep 10,935 m ± 6 m. Trench length and pressure from NOAA. First reached by Jacques Piccard and Don Walsh in the Trieste, 1960.
